record.paper_title: 25 Open Questions About Vector Bundles and Their Moduli
record.context_brief: Fundamental groups of instanton and bundle moduli
record.original_question: For a complex surface X, what is the fundamental group of the moduli space of instantons on X, or equivalently of the corresponding moduli space of holomorphic vector bundles when the Kobayashi-Hitchin correspondence applies?

evidence.quote: Question 25. What is the fundamental group of the moduli space of instantons (or holomorphic bundles) on X?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth compact complex surface equipped with a Hermitian metric (for instance, a Kähler surface). Fix a smooth complex vector bundle $E \to X$ of rank $r$ together with topological invariants (rank, Chern classes $c_1, c_2$). Consider the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{inst}}(X, E)$ of irreducible anti-self-dual (Hermitian–Einstein) connections on $E$ modulo gauge equivalence. When the Kobayashi–Hitchin correspondence applies, this moduli space is homeomorphic to the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{hol}}(X, E)$ of isomorphism classes of stable holomorphic vector bundle structures on $E$ with the prescribed topological type.

Determine the fundamental group $\pi_1\!\left(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{inst}}(X, E)\right) \;\cong\; \pi_1\!\left(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{hol}}(X, E)\right)$ in terms of invariants of $X$ (such as $\pi_1(X)$, the Hodge numbers, and the Chern classes of $E$). In particular, give a general formula or structural description of this fundamental group, valid across the relevant classes of complex surfaces $X$ for which the moduli space is non-empty and well-behaved.
artifact.category_tag: Moduli of vector bundles and instantons
artifact.status_search_result: The general question of computing the fundamental group of moduli spaces of instantons (or stable holomorphic bundles) on an arbitrary complex surface appears to remain open. Partial results exist in special cases (e.g., simple connectivity in certain rank-2 moduli on specific surfaces, and known computations for moduli on curves), but no general answer for arbitrary complex surfaces is established in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: 25 open questions about vector bundles and their moduli (E. Ballico)
status_evidence.snippet: Question 25. What is the fundamental group of the moduli space of instantons (or holomorphic bundles) on X?
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open problem in a list of open questions on vector bundle moduli.

status_evidence.title: An introduction to the topology of the moduli space of stable bundles
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of topology of moduli of stable bundles, including connectivity and homotopy results in special cases.
status_evidence.claim: Topological invariants of moduli of stable bundles are known in particular cases (e.g. curves), but no general formula for surfaces is given.

status_evidence.title: Moduli Spaces of PU(2) instantons
status_evidence.snippet: Studies geometry/topology of PU(2) instanton moduli spaces on complex surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Topology of instanton moduli on surfaces is studied case-by-case rather than via a general formula.
